picks.thesis: Cash-generative low-beta defensive with pricing power against 3.3% core PCE. Pipeline repricing (Phase 3 cancer-vaccine win, sac-TMT, Winrevair +75%) is upside optionality inside a 3-6mo window, while the Keytruda LOE sits in 2028 — outside it.
picks.verifiedFromFilings: Q2-2026 8-K: Keytruda/QLEX $8.366bn of $16.6bn total sales = 50.4% single-product concentration. KEYTRUDA QLEX (subcutaneous, the LOE mitigant) only $463m = 5.5% of the franchise — early, not established.
falsifiers: a sac-TMT or intismeran Phase 3 readout misses
Keytruda erosion runs ahead of plan before 2028
QLEX conversion stalls below ~10% of the franchise by mid-2027
QLEX revenue fails to scale materially above ~5.5% of the Keytruda franchise over the next 2-3 quarters despite the mid-2026 approvals
picks.knownWeakness: Entry price $149.50 is ABOVE the ~$131 average analyst target cited in the August source I used, which quoted the stock at ~$121. The stock has already run +23% past the price my thesis was built on. Upside-to-target is negative at entry unless targets are revised up.

thesisRevised.trigger: Entry price ($149.50) checked against the source the thesis was built on (~$121, $131 avg target).
thesisRevised.whatChanged: The re-rating I described as PROSPECTIVE has largely already happened: +73% over the past year, +23% in the six weeks since that source. Targets were revised up repeatedly (HSBC 150->172, Leerink 127->161, Guggenheim 146->170, Wells Fargo 150->170), but the current 26-analyst AVERAGE is ~$148 against a ~$149 price — consensus upside is now approximately zero.
thesisRevised.revisedClaim: The thesis is no longer 'the market will re-rate the pipeline'. It is the narrower and harder claim that QLEX conversion executes from 5.5% of the franchise, and that the recent $161-172 targets are right while the $148 average is too low. Mid-2026 oncology approvals (bladder, TNBC, renal cell) are fresh, so revenue lags approvals — that is the specific thing that has to show up.
thesisRevised.rankingEffect: No longer a clear #1. The implied valuation cushion does not exist. NOT ranked against ROST with confidence, because there is no valuation data on either — the exact gap recorded in biggestGap, which bit the top pick.

picks.thesis: Structural, not cyclical, trade-down: post-2022 behaviour change with $100k+ households now shopping off-price. Keyed directly to verified macro — 3.3% inflation plus a softening labour market.
picks.verifiedFromFilings: Q2-2026 8-K: comps +10% driven PRIMARILY BY TRAFFIC (high-quality comp). But 405 of the 610bps operating-margin gain came from one-time IEEPA tariff refunds (~$253m, $1.60/sh); ex-refund +205bps vs a 130-150bps plan — underlying beat is real. Guidance DECELERATES: Q3 comps +6-7%, Q4 +4-5%. FY2025 10-K Item 1A: 'more than half of the goods we sell originate from China' but 'we directly import only a small portion' — tariff exposure is largely INDIRECT via vendor cost.
falsifiers: gross margin compresses on non-IEEPA (Sec 301/232) tariffs
consumer class actions over passed-through tariff costs gain traction
traffic growth turns negative (the comp becomes price-driven)
picks.knownWeakness: Most of the reported margin beat is non-recurring. Company's own risk factors name fuel, energy, rates and housing costs as consumer headwinds — the same inflation that drives trade-down also squeezes its customer.

picks.thesis: Best growth in the set: Q2-2026 revenue +24%, Cloud +82% to $24.8bn, Cloud operating income TRIPLED $2.83bn -> $8.81bn, operating margin 34%. AI capex is converting into contracted profitable revenue rather than depreciation.
picks.verifiedFromFilings: Q2-2026 8-K cash statement: operating cash flow $39.1bn (+41% YoY) but capex $44.9bn (+100%) => FREE CASH FLOW -$5.9bn, versus +$5.3bn a year earlier. Buybacks $0 versus $13.2bn. Trailing four quarters of FCF: $24.5bn -> $24.6bn -> $10.1bn -> -$5.9bn (a trend, not a blip); TTM FCF still +$53.3bn. Depreciation +43% and accelerating.
falsifiers: Cloud growth decelerates below ~40% while capex stays elevated
FCF stays negative for two more quarters with buybacks still suspended
an adverse antitrust remedy in search or ad tech
server useful-life extension flatters earnings while cash keeps deteriorating
picks.knownWeakness: Ranked 3rd not 1st ONLY on cash profile. Negative-and-falling FCF with capital returns suspended is the wrong shape for a hiking cycle at a 0.02% risk premium. If optimising for absolute return rather than risk-adjusted, this is arguably the best pick — flagged as a judgment call, not a fact.

picks.thesis: Asset-light freight forwarder monetising disruption — emergency surcharges, Red Sea diversion, the 25-30% Cape of Good Hope premium. Q1 EPS +16%, Q2 +51%.
picks.verifiedFromFilings: NOT VERIFIED FROM FILINGS. Thesis rests on secondary sources only. The EPS bridge (price vs volume vs buyback) and net revenue per shipment were never checked.
falsifiers: Hormuz normalises and air/ocean spot rates revert to pre-conflict
a quarter where tonnage grows but EPS does not (price, not volume, was the driver)
EIA's de-escalation path plays out: Brent to ~$77 by 2Q27
picks.knownWeakness: Bets AGAINST the consensus de-escalation, and is CORRELATED with energy names — both are 'disruption persists' trades. Weakest evidentiary base of the five.

picks.thesis: Negative beta is genuinely rare and is worth more than upside in a multiple-compression scenario. Verified pricing power: late-2025 pricing actions delivering both volume and revenue growth.
picks.verifiedFromFilings: NOT VERIFIED FROM FILINGS. Unit case volume — the number that separates real pricing power from a value trap — was never checked.
falsifiers: unit case volume turns negative (pricing without volume)
the defensive rotation reverses and beta turns positive
FX drag on a strong dollar overwhelms pricing
picks.knownWeakness: Explicitly the hedge, not the idea. +26% YTD and sources say the thesis is largely priced in. Lowest expected upside of the five, held for its correlation property.

rejectedTheses.why: Brent peaked $113, already ~$100, EIA models $77 by 2Q27. Buying a shock after the peak into live mediation.
Property-cat reinsurance rates FELL 14.7% at Jan-2026 renewals, largest since 2014, on record $700bn+ capital. Property is softening.
Q1-2026 was the first NII decline since mid-2024, and most bullish sources assume CUTS — they predate the September hike.
Index +150% since 2020 at elevated valuations; 2026 earnings-growth expectations fell 15%->12%; munitions replenishment is a production-constrained 3-5 year project; no durable war lift.
Zero names pass on any quality basis, and it is the most rate-sensitive sector in a hiking cycle.

biggestGap: No valuation data anywhere in this analysis or in the repo. Not a P/E, not an FCF yield, not an EV/EBITDA. With the equity risk premium at 0.02%, valuation is the single most decision-relevant variable and it is the one thing neither the screen nor this research computed.
